proof: Take line ell as x-axis, half wedge angle alpha, centers on the interior bisector of the pictured common wedge. A radius-r sphere tangent to both planes has center distance r*csc(alpha) from ell. The two equal radius36 centers have x separation72, at x=+-36; tangency forces the radius13 center to x=0. Its distance49 to each large center gives36^2+(36-13)^2*csc(alpha)^2=49^2. Hence csc^2(alpha)=1105/529 and cot(alpha)=24/23. A perpendicular cross-section gives distance from ell to a tangency foot on either plane r*cot(alpha)=312/23. gcd312,23=1, so m+n=335. Assuming perpendicular planes would give13 (sum14), but violates the three sphere tangencies:36^2+2*23^2=2354 !=2401. The actual desired foot is neither a silhouette nor an equator point in the frozen projection.
